rationale:
structural: The only structural obligation is the prescribed signature: `impl<'d, D: Domain> ValidationContext<'d, D> { pub fn graph(&self) -> &'d D; }`. An alternative that returns `&D` tied to the `&self` borrow would behave the same at runtime but would not have this signature, so the signature is binding. The prose, "Borrow the application domain", is satisfied by returning the stored reference. The note about bypassing dependency tracking is a caveat, not an obligation.

The root `crates/trust-but-verify/src/procedure.rs#impl[ValidationContext<'d, D>]#2/fn[graph]` is in an `impl<'d, D: Domain> ValidationContext<'d, D>` block. It declares `pub fn graph(&self) -> &'d D` and returns `self.graph`. It matches the prescribed signature and is marked {impl} for this requirement. No other roots need markers.

behavioral: `ValidationContext.graph` has two behavioral obligations. `graph()` must return a borrow of the same domain the context was built with. Calls made directly on that domain must bypass dependency tracking.

Both are checked in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[snapshots_record_exact_reads_and_retain_distinct_versions]`, which carries a `{test}` reference to this requirement:
- **Same domain:** `assert!(std::ptr::eq(inspection.graph(), &graph))` shows `graph()` returns the very domain passed to `ValidationContext::new`.
- **Bypass:** the test calls `inspection.graph().node_content(...)` directly and asserts `inspection.dependencies().is_empty()`. A `graph()` that recorded dependencies on direct calls would fail here.
- **Tracked reads still work:** the test then clears the domain's read log and does a tracked `inspection.read(...)`. It asserts that this read is recorded, so the empty-dependency result above is not an artifact. The later `reads` log assertion also shows the domain was reached.

The `'d` lifetime of the returned reference is enforced by the compiler, so it needs no runtime test. `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` also checks the public export inventory and that the `habeas` consumer compiles against the SDK. I found no gaps.
